title.value: GitHub Repositories with Links to Academic Papers: Public Access, Traceability, and Evolution
title.justification: The title precisely reflects the content of the paper, focusing on GitHub repositories and their connections with academic papers regarding public access, traceability, and evolution.
title.quote: GitHub Repositories with Links to Academic Papers: Public Access, Traceability, and Evolution

extractions.description: This paper investigates the role of academic paper references contained in GitHub repositories, conducting a large-scale study of 20 thousand repositories that reference academic papers. It evaluates public access, traceability, and the evolution of these links, finding that while few papers link back to the repositories, a large portion of referenced papers are publicly accessible and often related to machine learning topics.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily deals with the traceability and evolution of links between GitHub repositories and academic papers, which is not directly related to Climate Change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Traceability between published scientific breakthroughs and their implementation is essential, especially in the case of open-source scientific software which implements bleeding-edge science in its code.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any of the predefined Climate Change categories. It centers around software engineering and academic paper traceability.
primary_category.quote: This paper investigates the role of academic paper references contained in these repositories. We conduct a large-scale study of 20 thousand GitHub repositories that make references to academic papers.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address any secondary Climate Change themes. Its focus remains on the relationship and traceability of academic papers in GitHub repositories.
secondary_categories.quote: In this paper, we lay the foundation for understanding the role of links to academic papers in GitHub repositories by collecting 20,278 GitHub repositories created between 2014 and 2018.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category of Climate Change is addressed in this paper, as its focus lies outside the Climate Change scope.
primary_sub_category.quote: The main goal of our study is to gain insights into the links between software repositories on GitHub and academic papers, and to uncover potential issues related to public access, traceability, and evolution.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not map to any secondary sub-categories under Climate Change.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Summary: With more than 20,000 GitHub repositories that reference an academic paper, the phenomenon is worthy of further exploration.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new Climate Change category, as it does not focus on Climate Change.
new_primary_category.quote: Although these papers are complementary, to the best of our knowledge, the link between repositories and papers has not been studied comprehensively.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: To understand public access, traceability, and evolution of links to academic papers in GitHub repositories, we conducted (i) a quantitative study of around 20 thousand links from GitHub README.mds.
